comments.headline: Missing legend definitions for boundary symbols
comments.summary: Multiple boundary elements are depicted on plan sheets but lack distinct symbol definitions in the legend. Easement types, Right-of-Way boundary, and floodplain boundaries must each have defined line types per LDC § 25-7-33(D)(3) and UCM 2.5.1.E.9.

details.text: The legend defines only a generic 'Easement' or '-PUE-' symbol, but six distinct easement types are shown on plan sheets (Drainage, Wastewater, Water, Electric, Telephone, Sidewalk Easements, and Public Utility Easements). Each type must have its own distinct linetype and symbol definition in the legend.

runComments.comment: Easement line types are not adequately defined in the plan legend. Multiple distinct easement types are depicted on the plans (Drainage Easement, Wastewater Easement, Water Easement, Electric Easement, Telephone Easement, Sidewalk Easement) but the legend defines only a generic 'Easement' symbol with '-PUE-' linetype. Each easement type shown on the plans must have a distinct, defined linetype in the legend.

Multiple distinct easement types are shown on the site plan sheets (Drainage Easement, Wastewater Easement, Water Easement/Vault Easement, Sidewalk Easement, Public Utility Easement, Electric Easement), but the legend defines only a generic 'Easement' symbol (dashed line with PUE text). Each easement type shown on the plans must have its own defined linetype and symbol in the legend to clearly differentiate easement categories.

The legend defines general "Existing Easement" and "Easement (PUE)" symbols but does not explicitly define a specific linetype for drainage easements. LDC § 25-7-33(D)(3) requires distinct linetype definitions for drainage easements in the plan legend.

details.text: Right-of-Way boundary symbol and linetype are not included in the plan legend, although the ROW is referenced on plan sheets (e.g., 'Valley View Road 50' R.O.W.'). UCM 2.5.1.E.9 requires the ROW boundary to be defined in the legend with distinct symbol and linetype designation.

runComments.comment: Right-of-Way boundary symbol is not included in the plan legend. UCM 2.5.1.E.9 requires that all boundary elements including ROW boundaries be defined in the plan legend with appropriate symbol and linetype designations. The legend must include a distinct ROW boundary symbol.

The Right-of-Way (ROW) boundary symbol is not included in the site plan legend. UCM 2.5.1.E.9 requires ROW dimensions and legend definitions on all Austin Water civil plan sheets. Add ROW boundary linetype and symbol to the legend.

Right-of-Way (ROW) boundary symbol is not included in the plan legend on Sheet 3. While the ROW is labeled as text ("Valley View Road 50' R.O.W.") on plan sheets, the ROW boundary linetype must be defined in the legend.

details.text: The legend defines only a generic '100 yr' linetype for floodplain boundaries without distinguishing between City of Austin 100-year floodplain and FEMA floodplain. LDC § 25-7-33(D)(3) requires both floodplain types to be depicted with distinct, defined linetypes in the legend.

runComments.comment: The legend defines only the City of Austin 100-year floodplain ('100 yr' linetype) but does not separately define the FEMA floodplain linetype. LDC § 25-7-33(D)(3) requires both the City of Austin 100-year floodplain and the FEMA floodplain to be depicted with distinct, defined linetypes in the plan legend. Add FEMA floodplain symbol and linetype to the legend, clearly distinguished from the local 100-year floodplain.

Floodplain line types in the legend show only "100 yr" without distinction between City of Austin 100-year floodplain and FEMA floodplain. LDC § 25-7-33(D)(3) requires that the City of Austin 100-year floodplain and FEMA floodplain be shown separately on plan sheets with distinct linetypes defined in the legend.

comments.headline: Missing delineated linework for recorded easements and floodplains
comments.summary: Multiple recorded easements and floodplain boundaries documented in property records and public databases are not depicted as drawn linework on site plan sheets. The Greenbelt Access & Use Easement (recorded), City of Austin and FEMA floodplain boundaries, and recorded drainage easements from subdivision plats must be delineated per LDC § 25-7-33(D)(3) and UCM 2.5.1.E.11.
comments.crossDep: Surveyor (for easement boundary verification and documentation); Austin Water (for recorded easement records validation)
comments.attn: Verify recorded easement instruments (Greenbelt Access & Use Easement 2010070731; Cortez Heights plat Vol 64/13 C8-71-079; Trico Subdivision plat Vol 69/14 C8S-74-075) with current property survey and Austin Water records. Confirm floodplain boundaries with current FEMA and City of Austin flood data.

details.text: Greenbelt Access & Use Easement (Recorded Instrument 2010070731), a perpetual no-build easement covering 0.31 acres in the NE interior of Lot 1, is not shown as delineated boundaries on ESC Plan, Site Plan, or Grading Plan sheets. Additionally, City of Austin 100-year and FEMA floodplain boundaries are not depicted as drawn linework, though project location is outside FEMA Zone X per cover sheet. Drainage easements from Cortez Heights plat (Vol 64/13: 25' Drainage Easement and 7.5' PUE) and Trico Subdivision plat (Vol 69/14: 10' Drainage Easement) identified in property records are not verified on submitted site plan.

runComments.comment: The Greenbelt Access & Use Easement (Recorded Instrument 2010070731), a perpetual no-build easement covering 0.31 acres in the NE interior of Lot 1, is not depicted as delineated linework on any site plan sheets. This recorded easement must be shown with delineated boundaries on all applicable plan sheets per UCM 2.5.1.E.11 requirement to show all existing infrastructure within the Limits of Construction.

Neither the City of Austin 100-year floodplain boundary nor the FEMA floodplain boundary is depicted as delineated linework on any site plan sheet. Although the project location is outside the 100-year floodplain (FEMA Zone X per cover sheet), LDC § 25-7-33(D)(3) explicitly requires every site plan—including those outside floodplain areas—to affirmatively show (a) the City of Austin 100-year floodplain and (b) the FEMA floodplain as distinct delineated boundaries with linework, not merely in the legend. Add both floodplain boundaries to the appropriate plan sheets with distinct, defined linetypes.

Drainage easements recorded on the Cortez Heights plat (Vol 64/13, C8-71-079) and Trico Subdivision plat (Vol 69/14, C8S-74-075) are not properly depicted with complete recording instrument numbers on the plan sheets. The 25' Drainage Easement and 7.5' PUE from Vol 64/13 and the 10' Drainage Easement from Vol 69/14 identified in the property records are not verified on the submitted site plan. LDC § 25-7-33(D)(3) requires all recorded drainage easements to be depicted as delineated linework.

comments.headline: Missing building labels and street addresses
comments.summary: Building footprints lack required identification: street addresses, use/function designation, existing vs. proposed status, and unit types. Structures are identified only by building number and unit numbers (Unit 101-806), not by street address or use. UCM 2.5.1.E.14 and BCM 1.2.7 require complete building identification on site and utility plan sheets.
comments.crossDep: Addressing Services (for street address format and unit numbering confirmation per COA Addressing Standards)
comments.attn: Confirm street address format with Austin Address Management Services. Verify multi-family unit numbering convention and unit type designations (Two-Bedroom vs. Three-Bedroom distribution across buildings).

details.text: Buildings 1-8 are identified only by building number and unit numbers (Unit 101-806) on site plan (Sheet 9) and utility tap plan (Sheet 19), but no street address appears for any building. Per UCM 2.5.1.E.14, all structures must be labeled with street address on utility plan sheets. Expected format: 3759 Valley View Road, Unit [number].

runComments.comment: Street address for each building structure is not shown on the Austin Water utility plan sheet. Buildings 1-8 are identified only by building number and unit numbers on Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan), but no street address is visible for any building. Per UCM 2.5.1.E.14, the street address for all structures must appear on the lot where the structures are located on Austin Water utility plan sheets.

Buildings are labeled with unit numbers only (e.g., 'Unit 101', 'Unit 102') on the site plan and addressing plan sheets. UCM 2.5.1.E.14 requires the street address for all existing and proposed structures to appear on the lot(s) where structures are located on Austin Water utility plan sheets. For this multi-family project with 39 units, each building footprint must be labeled with its assigned street address in the format: 3759 Valley View Road, Unit [number] (or equivalent format confirmed with Address Management Services).

Street addresses are not labeled on building structures on the site plan or addressing plan. Only building numbers (Bldg. 1-8) and unit numbers (Unit 101-806) are shown. Per UCM 2.5.1.E.14, the street address for all structures must appear on the lot(s) where the structures are located on utility plan sheets.

details.text: Building use (Multi-Family Residential) is identified only in data tables on plan sheets, not labeled directly on building footprints. BCM 1.2.7 requires that site plans show building location and size with use identification labeled on structures.

runComments.comment: Building use or function (Multi-Family Residential) is not labeled directly on building footprints on the site plan. Use information appears only in data tables on the plan sheet, not as direct labels on structures. Per BCM 1.2.7, site plan must show building location and size with use identification.

details.text: Proposed buildings (Bldg. 1-8) are not labeled 'Proposed,' while adjacent existing buildings are labeled 'Existing Apartment Building.' UCM 2.5.1.E.11 requires consistent labeling of existing versus proposed improvements on all site plans.

runComments.comment: Existing versus proposed status is not labeled consistently. Existing adjacent buildings are labeled "Existing Apartment Building," but proposed buildings (Bldg. 1-8) are not labeled "Proposed" - only identified by building numbers. UCM 2.5.1.E.11 requires consistent labeling of existing versus proposed improvements.

details.text: Unit types (Two-Bedroom and Three-Bedroom) are not labeled on building structures on site plan (Sheet 9) or addressing plan (Sheet 29). Only unit numbers (Unit 101-806) are shown; unit type designations do not appear on the plans. Per City of Austin Addressing Standards, unit types must be labeled for multi-family residential projects.

runComments.comment: Unit types (Two-Bedroom and Three-Bedroom) are not labeled on the site plan for multi-family residential buildings. Only unit numbers (Unit 101-806) are shown; unit types are not identified on the plans. Per City of Austin Addressing Standards, unit types must be labeled on site plan for multi-family residential projects.

comments.headline: Property boundary inconsistencies across discipline sheets
comments.summary: Property boundary lines show three problems: absent from the landscape plan, inconsistent bearings recorded across sheets, and inconsistent linetypes between sheets. UCM 2.5.1.E.9 requires property boundaries on all applicable civil plan sheets with consistent dimensions and symbology matching the recorded Mecey Subdivision plat (Vol. 73, Pg. 76).
comments.crossDep: Surveyor (for boundary dimension verification and bearing reconciliation against recorded subdivision plat)
comments.attn: Verify all property boundary dimensions and bearings against recorded Mecey Subdivision plat (Vol. 73, Pg. 76). Resolve bearing discrepancies (N62°36'57"W vs. N63°36'57"W vs. N63°39'57") and confirm property survey is current. Verify landscape plan includes property boundaries.

details.text: Property boundary lines appear on site plan (Sheet 9), grading plan (Sheet 11), ESC plan (Sheet 5), utility plan (Sheet 19), and addressing plan (Sheet 29) sheets, but are absent from the landscape plan (Sheet 31). UCM 2.5.1.E.9 requires property boundaries to appear on all applicable civil plan sheets.

runComments.comment: Property boundary lines are shown on site plan, grading plan, ESC plan, utility plan, and addressing plan, but are absent from the landscape plan. Property boundaries must appear on all applicable civil plan sheets per UCM 2.5.1.E.9.

details.text: Property boundary bearings show inconsistencies across sheets: N62°36'57"W on Sheet 9 (Site Plan), N63°39'57"W on Sheet 8, and N63°36'57"W on Sheet 29 (Addressing Plan) for the same boundary segment. All property boundary dimensions and bearings must match the recorded Mecey Subdivision plat (Vol. 73, Pg. 76) and discrepancies must be resolved with clarification notes or updated survey.

runComments.comment: Property boundary bearings show inconsistencies across sheets: Sheet 9 shows N62°36'57"W, Sheet 8 shows N63°39'57"W, and Sheet 29 shows N63°36'57"W for nominally the same boundary segment. Verify that all property boundary dimensions and bearings match the recorded Mecey Subdivision plat (Vol. 73, Pg. 76) and resolve discrepancies with clarification notes or a revised survey.

details.text: Property boundary linetype is inconsistent across discipline sheets: depicted as a heavy dash-dot line on Sheet 9 (Site Plan) but as a solid line on Sheet 11 (Grading Plan). All boundary linework must use consistent symbology throughout all discipline sheets per reviewer convention.

runComments.comment: Property boundary linetype is inconsistent across plan sheets. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) depicts the property boundary as a heavy dash-dot line, while Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) depicts it as a solid line. Property boundary linework must use consistent symbology throughout all discipline sheets.
